'''Edl Schamiloglu''' (born 1959) is an American [[physicist]], [[Electrical engineering|electrical engineer]], [[pulsed power]] expert, [[Invention|inventor]], and [[distinguished professor]] in the department of electrical and computer engineering at the [[University of New Mexico]].<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Edl Schamiloglu - Electrical & Computer Engineering - The University of New Mexico |url=http://www.ece.unm.edu/faculty-staff/electrical-and-computer/edl-schamiloglu.html |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=www.ece.unm.edu}}</ref> He has been known in public media for his expertise in the design and operation of [[directed-energy weapon]]s.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gugliotta |first=Guy |date=2003-03-19 |title=Military May Microwave Iraqi Electronic Circuits |language=en-US |newspaper=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/2003/03/19/military-may-microwave-iraqi-electronic-circuits/699f728e-da85-4410-9144-49272da91cd3/ |access-date=2021-08-21 |issn=0190-8286}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Schiesel |first=Seth |date=2003-02-20 |title=Taking Aim at an Enemy's Chips |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/02/20/technology/taking-aim-at-an-enemy-s-chips.html |access-date=2021-08-18 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Abrams |first=Michael |title=Dawn of the E-Bomb |url=http://ece-research.unm.edu/schamiloglu/EdlPDF/SpectrumArticle.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326182309/http://ece-research.unm.edu:80/schamiloglu/EdlPDF/SpectrumArticle.pdf |archive-date=2017-03-26 |website=unm.edu}}</ref> He is also known for his assessment on the possible origins of alleged health damages presumably caused on U.S. embassy personnel in [[Cuba]] in 2016 as part of the [[Havana syndrome]] incident.<ref>{{Cite book |last=National Academies of Sciences |first=Engineering |url=https://www.nap.edu/catalog/25889/an-assessment-of-illness-in-us-government-employees-and-their-families-at-overseas-embassies |title=An Assessment of Illness in U.S. Government Employees and Their Families at Overseas Embassies |date=2020-12-05 |publisher=National Academies Press |isbn=978-0-309-68137-7 |language=en}}</ref> He is the founding director of the recently launched [[University of New Mexico|UNM Directed Energy Center]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Directed Energy Center at UNM {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=https://dec.unm.edu/ |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=dec.unm.edu}}</ref> Schamiloglu is a book author and co-editor, and has received numerous awards for his academic achievements. He is a Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]]<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Nuclear & Plasma Sciences Society {{!}} Fellows Committee |url=https://ieee-npss.org/fellows-committee/ |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=ieee-npss.org}}</ref> and the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=Schamiloglu elected as a Fellow of American Physical Society :: School of Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=http://engineering.unm.edu/news/2020/09/schamiloglu-named-elected-as-a-fellow-of-american-physical-society.html |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=engineering.unm.edu}}</ref> Starting on July 1, 2024, Schamiloglu was selected as [[Editor-in-chief|Editor-in-Chief]] of the [[IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science]], where he succeeds Steven J. Gitomer who has held that role for over 40 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Schamiloglu selected as editor in chief of 'IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science' :: School of Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=http://engineering.unm.edu/news/2024/03/schamiloglu-selected-as-editor-in-chief-of-ieee-transactions-on-plasma-science.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=engineering.unm.edu}}</ref> In July 2025 he was appointed a Nonresident Fellow, ''Center for Disruptive Technology and Future Warfare'', [[National Defense University (United States)|National Defense University]], Washington, DC.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Edl Schamiloglu, Non-Resident Fellow, CDTFW |url=https://inss.ndu.edu/Media/Biographies/Article-View/Article/4285684/edl-schamiloglu/ |access-date=Sep 19, 2025 |website=[[National Defense University (Washington, D.C.)|National Defense University]]}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Schamiloglu was born in [[The Bronx]] in 1959 to [[Tatars|Tatar]]{{citation needed|date=September 2026}} parents from Russia who wed in [[Istanbul]] in 1957, where their families had independently arrived as political refugees.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Delker |first=Kim |date=Oct 26, 2020 |title=66 semesters on Route 66 and still going strong |url=http://ece-research.unm.edu/schamiloglu/EdlPDF/66%20semesters%20on%20Route%2066%20Optimized.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210820082300/http://ece-research.unm.edu/schamiloglu/EdlPDF/66%20semesters%20on%20Route%2066%20Optimized.pdf |archive-date=2021-08-20 |website=[[University of New Mexico]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=THE TATAR GAZETTE |url=http://tatar.yuldash.com/189.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050414084148/http://tatar.yuldash.com:80/189.html |archive-date=2005-04-14 |access-date=2021-08-21 |website=tatar.yuldash.com}}</ref> His only brother, Uli Schamiloglu, is professor and chair of the department of [[Kazakh language|Kazakh Language]] and [[Turkic peoples|Turkic]] Studies at [[Nazarbayev University]] in [[Nur-Sultan|Nursultan, Kazakhstan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Uli Schamiloglu |url=https://nu.edu.kz/faculty/uli-schamiloglu |access-date=2021-08-31 |website=Nazarbayev University |language=en-US |archive-date=2021-04-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419124219/https://nu.edu.kz/faculty/uli-schamiloglu }}</ref>

Schamiloglu attended the [[Bronx High School of Science]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1979, he obtained a Bachelor of Science in [[applied physics]] and [[applied mathematics]] and in 1981 a Master of Science degree in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] from [[Columbia University]]. In 1988, he earned a PhD in [[engineering]] (with a minor in [[mathematics]]) from [[Cornell University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-10-30 |title=Program Notes: Graduate Alumni |url=https://magazine.engineering.columbia.edu/fall-2018/program-notes |access-date=2021-08-19 |website=Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=A report from the School of ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING • Cornell University |url=https://cpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.coecis.cornell.edu/dist/a/151/files/2017/06/Plasma-Physics-Research-1997-p4v0yv.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615091239/https://cpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.coecis.cornell.edu/dist/a/151/files/2017/06/Plasma-Physics-Research-1997-p4v0yv.pdf |archive-date=2018-06-15 |website=wpmucdn.com}}</ref>

== Career ==
Schamiloglu has been a faculty member at [[University of New Mexico]] since 1988. At the UNM School of Engineering, he has successively been Regents' Lecturer from 1996 to 1999, ECE Gardner-Zemke Professor at the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department (since 2000),<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Schamiloglu honored with IEEE pulsed power award |url=http://news.unm.edu/news/schamiloglu-honored-with-ieee-pulsed-power-award |access-date=2021-08-21 |website=UNM Newsroom |language=en}}</ref> and distinguished professor since 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Two Engineering professors earn distinguished professor rank :: School of Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=http://engineering.unm.edu/news/2014/06/two-engineering-professors-earn-distinguished-professor-rank.html |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=engineering.unm.edu}}</ref> Also at the University of New Mexico, he has been associate chair and director of the Graduate Program (2000–2001), director of the School of Engineering Research Center COSMIAC (2015-2017), associate dean for research and innovation (2017-2023), and special assistant to the provost for laboratory relations (2018-2025).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Schamiloglu appointed Special Assistant to the Provost for Laboratory Relations |url=http://news.unm.edu/news/schamiloglu-appointed-special-assistant-to-the-provost-for-laboratory-relations |access-date=2021-08-18 |website=UNM Newsroom |language=en}}</ref> He is also president of the ''SUMMA Foundation'', an independent, philanthropic organization promoting  scientific and educational activities in the field of [[Electromagnetism|electromagnetics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SUMMA Foundation - Carl Baum, Electrical and Computer Engineering Department, University of New Mexico |url=https://ece-research.unm.edu/summa/ |access-date=2024-06-13 |website=ece-research.unm.edu}}</ref>

At University of New Mexico, he established a program for research and education in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma science]] involving [[pulsed power]] and intense beam-driven, high power microwave devices. He founded the Pulsed Power, Beams and Microwaves Laboratory (1989), where for many years his team have been pursuing research in areas such as modeling of electromagnetic systems, directed energy microwaves, and the effects of high power microwaves on systems.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research Laboratories :: Electrical & Computer Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=https://ece.unm.edu/research/research-laboratories.html |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=ece.unm.edu}}</ref>

Acting as a principal investigator, or leading multilateral alliances, Schamiloglu's laboratory has received research subsidies of millions of dollars often originating from the [[United States Department of Defense|US Department of Defense]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Justin |date=Apr 17, 2001 |title=UNM wins $5 million defense research grant |url=http://ece-research.unm.edu/schamiloglu/EdlPDF/muri.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326175941/http://ece-research.unm.edu:80/schamiloglu/EdlPDF/muri.pdf |archive-date=2017-03-26 |website=unm.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Research Team Led by ECE Professor Edl Schamiloglu Awarded Prestigious MURI Grant |url=http://news.unm.edu/news/research-team-led-by-ece-professor-edl-schamiloglu-awarded-prestigious-muri-grant |access-date=2021-08-21 |website=UNM Newsroom |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Schamiloglu awarded more than $1.4 million in Department of Defense grants |url=http://news.unm.edu/news/schamiloglu-awarded-more-than-1-4-million-in-department-of-defense-grants |access-date=2021-08-23 |website=UNM Newsroom |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Service |first=Kim Delker {{!}} UNM News |date=13 April 2020 |title=UNM professor heads team winning $7.5M grant |url=https://www.abqjournal.com/1442982/unm-professor-heads-team-winning-75m-grant.html |access-date=2021-08-21 |website=www.abqjournal.com |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2020, he led a five-university inter-institutional team sponsored by the Air Force, which was selected for a [[MURI (grant)|Multidisciplinary University Research Initiative (MURI) Award]] from the [[United States Department of Defense]] to explore the ''Fundamental Limits to High Power Electromagnetic Amplification.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=FY2020 MULTIDISCIPLINARY UNIVERSITY RESEARCH INITIATIVE (MURI) - SELECTED PROJECTS |url=https://www.cto.mil/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/fy2020-muri-press-release.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021093724/https://www.cto.mil/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/fy2020-muri-press-release.pdf |archive-date=2020-10-21 |website=www.cto.mil}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=UNM Engineering professor leads team to win MURI award for research :: School of Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=http://engineering.unm.edu/news/2020/03/unm-engineering-professor-leads-team-to-win-muri-award-for-research.html |access-date=2021-08-21 |website=engineering.unm.edu}}</ref>

As a [[Principal investigator|principal co-investigator]], Schamiloglu became a founding member of the NSF Directorate for Engineering's sponsored Engineering Research Visioning Alliance (ERVA), together with [[Dorota Grejner-Brzezińska]] from The Ohio State University (now Research Vice-chancelor at [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|UW Madison]]),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dorota A. Grejner-Brzezinska named UW–Madison vice chancellor for research |url=https://news.wisc.edu/dorota-a-grejner-brzezinska-named-uw-madison-vice-chancellor-for-research/ |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=news.wisc.edu |date=7 May 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref> Anthony Boccanfuso from the University Industry Demonstration Partnership (UIDP), Barry W. Johnson from the University of Virginia, and Charles Johnson-Bey, of [[Booz Allen Hamilton]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=UNM part of NSF's Engineering Research Visioning Alliance |url=http://news.unm.edu/news/unm-part-of-nsfs-engineering-research-visioning-alliance |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=UNM Newsroom |language=en}}</ref> Johnson's position at ERVA was later filled by [[Pramod P. Khargonekar|Pramod Khargonekar]] from the [[University of California, Irvine]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Homepage - Pramod Khargonekar |url=https://faculty.sites.uci.edu/khargonekar/ |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=faculty.sites.uci.edu}}</ref>

Schamiloglu has taught electromagnetics, plasma physics, neurosystems engineering, and advanced mathematics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Edl Schamiloglu - School of Engineering - The University of New Mexico |url=https://engineering.unm.edu/faculty/directory/electrical-and-computer/edl-schamiloglu.html |access-date=2021-08-21 |website=engineering.unm.edu}}</ref> He has been an invited lecturer at institutions in the US, UK, India and China. He has supervised over eighty [[Master of Science|M.S.]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] dissertations in related fields. Also, his laboratory has hosted many international visiting scientists since 1991.<ref name=":2" />

As a special assistant to the provost, Schamiloglu aided in the development of working relations between the University of New Mexico and [[United States Department of Energy national laboratories]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Edl Schamiloglu |url=http://ece-research.unm.edu/schamiloglu/ |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=ece-research.unm.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=UNM and Sandia National Labs sign strategic alliance agreement |url=http://news.unm.edu/news/unm-and-sandia-national-labs-sign-strategic-alliance-agreement |access-date=2021-08-21 |website=UNM Newsroom |language=en}}</ref>

In 2002, he was elected a Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] ([[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]]) "For contributions to the generation and propagation of intense pulsed charged particle beams."<ref name=":7" /> In 2020, he became a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=":9" />

=== Service ===
Schamiloglu has often been a committee member and chair at [[University of New Mexico|UNM]], [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] and [[National academy|National Academies]].<ref name=":2" /> He served on the external advisory board for [[Sandia National Laboratories]], REHEDS Foundation, Army's Extramural Basic Research Program in Electronics (ARO), K&A Wireless, Directed Energy Professional Society, Pulsed Power Conferences, Inc., SUMMA, and EPSCoR/IDeA Foundations.<ref name=":2" /> He was also founding member (2016-2020) of the Matter and Radiation at Extremes Editorial Advisory Board (an Open Access Journal).

=== Patents ===
Schamiloglu is a co-inventor of several patents for devices often related to the operation of [[Cavity magnetron|magnetrons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Edl Schamiloglu Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/edl-schamiloglu |access-date=2021-08-23 |website=patents.justia.com}}</ref>

== Honors ==
Schamiloglu's academic achievements have been recognized by many awards. Within [[University of New Mexico|UNM]] he received Research Excellence Awards in 1992, 2001 and 2017, also Creativity Awards in 2011, 2012, 2013, 2018 and 2019.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=STC.UNM Hosts Creative Awards to Celebrate Researchers and Patent Holders |url=http://news.unm.edu/news/stc-unm-hosts-creative-awards-to-celebrate-researchers-and-patent-holders |access-date=2021-08-19 |website=UNM Newsroom |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=2012 STC.UNM Creative Awards Ceremony to Honor UNM Inventors :: School of Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=https://engineering.unm.edu/news/2012/04/2012-stc.unm-creative-awards-ceremony-to-honor-unm-inventors.html |access-date=2021-08-19 |website=engineering.unm.edu}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Success Stories, Center for Excellence |url=http://ece-research.unm.edu/AFOSR-COE/success.html |access-date=2021-08-19 |website=ece-research.unm.edu}}</ref> He was selected as a UNM Academic Leadership Fellow from 2013 to 2015,<ref name=":1" /> and received the Gardner-Zemke Research Award in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honors & Awards :: Electrical & Computer Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=https://ece.unm.edu/research/honors--awards.html |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=ece.unm.edu}}</ref>

Within the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] ([[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]]), his awards include:

* 2002: Elected Fellow "For Contributions to the Generation and Propagation of Intense Pulsed Charged Particle Beams"<ref name=":7" />
* 2008: Albuquerque Section Outstanding Engineering Educator Award
* 2013: Nuclear and Plasma Sciences Society's Richard F. Shea Distinguished Member Award "For Outstanding Contributions to its Technical Committees"<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nuclear & Plasma Sciences Society {{!}} Past Recipients of the Richard F. Shea Distinguished Member Award |url=https://ieee-npss.org/past-recipients-of-the-richard-f-shea-distinguished-member-award/ |access-date=2021-08-21 |website=ieee-npss.org}}</ref>
* 2015: NPSS PPST Peter Haas Award "For Research in the Area of Pulsed Power, Beams, and Microwaves, and for his Dedicated Service to the Current and Future Pulsed Power Community through his Leadership and Educational Endeavors"<ref name=":3" />
* 2019: Nuclear and Plasma Sciences Society's 2019 Magne "Kris" Kristiansen Award for Contributions to Experimental Nuclear and Plasma Science<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nuclear & Plasma Sciences Society {{!}} Past Recipients of the Magne "Kris" Kristiansen Award for Contributions to Experimental Nuclear and Plasma Science |url=https://ieee-npss.org/past-recipients-of-the-magne-kris-kristiansen-award-for-contributions-to-experimental-nuclear-and-plasma-science/ |access-date=2021-08-17 |website=ieee-npss.org}}</ref>

Other awards he has received include:

* 2003: City of Albuquerque [[Goodwill ambassador|Goodwill Ambassador]] Award<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 30, 2003 |title=Schamiloglu receives Ambassador Award |url=http://ece-research.unm.edu/schamiloglu/EdlPDF/goodwill.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326182317/http://ece-research.unm.edu:80/schamiloglu/EdlPDF/goodwill.pdf |archive-date=2017-03-26 |website=unm.edu}}</ref>
* 2011: CST (Journal) University Publication Award<ref>{{Cite web |title=CST University Publication Award 2011: Winners Announced |url=https://www.yumpu.com/en/document/read/12993545/cst-university-publication-award-2011-winners-announced |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=yumpu.com |language=en}}</ref>
* 2012: [[Air Force Research Laboratory|AFOSR]] 60th Anniversary Commemorative Medal for Leadership in Directed Energy<ref>{{Cite web |title=ECE Prof. Schamiloglu Presents at Air Force Anniversary Celebration :: School of Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico |url=https://engineering.unm.edu/news/2012/07/ece-prof.-schamiloglu-presents-at-air-force-anniversary-celebration.html |access-date=2021-08-22 |website=engineering.unm.edu}}</ref>
